election._note: Elected 1 November 2022 for a four-year term, so the next is due by November 2026; no fixed date announced, since the PM sets the polling day. 175 seats are Denmark proper plus two each from the Faroes and Greenland, which the register folds into one 179-seat chamber. Wikipedia, 'Next Danish general election'.

dissolution._note: The PM decides the polling day and advises the monarch, who dissolves the Folketing -- in practice an unfettered executive choice, Danish elections can and do come well before the four years are out, and there is no codified lockout; campaigns run about three weeks. Grundlov §7 and §32; Folketinget.dk, 'General elections'.

amendment._note: Grundlov §88: a constitutional amendment bill is passed by the Folketing, a general election is then called, the new Folketing must pass the bill again UNAMENDED, and it finally goes to a referendum within six months where approval needs a majority of votes cast AND at least 40% of every person entitled to vote. No single chamber supermajority exists anywhere in the procedure; the machinery's three_quarters carries the nearest entrenching number, and the interposed election and the confirmation referendum are not modelled as separate stages. Danmarks Riges Grundlov §88.
amendment._referendum_note: The §88 referendum is a MANDATORY stage of the real procedure rather than an option; the machinery's mandatory mode requires the referendum_required rule, which this system's template does not permit, so the confirmation is folded into the authored bar -- the same folding AUT.json records for Art. 44(3) and the Dutch file for its second reading.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: §88's procedure reaches every part of the constitution including the monarchy itself -- the 1953 abolition of the Landsting went through it -- so a system change runs at the same bar, not a higher one.

judicial._note: Hojesteret: the Supreme Court has asserted the power to strike statutes down as unconstitutional since its early-century case law, and the 1999 Tvind judgment did so outright -- rare in practice, but real, which is what the value records. Domstolene.dk; Wikipedia, 'Judicial review in Denmark'.

formation._note: The monarch appoints the statsminister after the post-election kongerunden talks between the party leaders, and Danish negative parliamentarism means a government never wins an investiture -- it survives while no majority votes against it. Grundlov §15: when a majority of the Folketing expresses no confidence in the Prime Minister, the PM must ask for the government's resignation or call an election, which is the machinery's simple_present. Folketinget.dk, 'The work of the Folketing'.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2024, rounded, on the same conventions as SVK.json's block. VAT 25% is the statutory standard rate, among Europe's highest (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'); corporate 22% is the statutory rate; income 26 is a blend of the municipal-plus-state schedule whose all-in top marginal sits near 56%, carried HIGH because Denmark's OECD Revenue Statistics personal-tax-to-GDP share is the OECD's heaviest, above even Belgium's; capital gains 27% is the standard share-income rate (42% above the threshold, folded to the lower). Wealth 0 -- the Danish wealth tax was abolished in 1997. Debt ~28.9% and revenue ~46.5% of GDP (Eurostat/OECD 2024). Spending is the general-government split scaled to expenditure near 48% of GDP.
